quest.title: A Search for Secrets
quest.description: While eating at Wanmin Restaurant, you encounter Yuandai and Shuyu. Yuandai, forgetful in her old age, cannot remember her past, but perhaps her having once been a chivalrous heroine is a good place to start...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Huh, it's you two... What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xingqiu! Great, we found you. We wanted to ask you about something!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the situation to Xingqiu.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hmm... That's not a whole lot of information to go off of. I don't know if I can say for sure.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I can't pinpoint her identity from your description alone. But considering her age, I am reminded of a "nameless heroine" who's been featured in various chivalric novels.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nameless heroine?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: That's right. The novels often speak of a great drought from fifty years ago. As the people suffered, a nameless heroine appeared and began to clear away evil spirits and bandit camps. The people idolized her but never learned her name.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: All they knew was that she always acted alone. Later, though, she supposedly fell in love with a similarly noble-minded exorcist from Mt. Tianheng. They were well-matched in more ways than one, often fighting together as a fearsome duo of otherworldly strength.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: After the drought ended, the heroine and the exorcist left the public eye and began living a reclusive life in the mountains. All that remained were tales of her incredible accomplishments.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: The way this nameless heroine faded from fame into obscurity later in life is not too dissimilar from Ms. Yuandai. I hope that's somewhat helpful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks a lot Xingqiu! We knew it'd be worth talking to you.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: It's nothing at all, just something I came across while reading. I did do a bit of extra research on her story, but it was just out of personal curiosity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon still thinks that's super cool! Wait, Xingqiu, if you've read up on her, do you know of any places often associated with her?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Let me think... In the novels, the nameless heroine always appeared near one of three places: Wangshu Inn, the area just north of Jueyun Karst, and Qingyun Peak.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Perhaps the real-life heroine who inspired the character was also often seen near those three places. That would explain why those locations appear in the various novels written about her.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Haha, you're welcome. To be honest, I found some parts of the story confusing when I first came across it. If Ms. Yuandai was indeed the original inspiration for the character, she may just be able to help me put the pieces together.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: It's rare for a chivalric hero to fade into obscurity during their lifetime, even after retiring from the public eye. But no one ever saw or heard from the nameless heroine again... There were even rumors that she became extremely ill.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I've never understood why someone would go to such lengths to erase themselves from public memory. It's almost as if she was trying to hide from something... There's probably far more to the story than what's been written.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll be sure to tell you if we manage to uncover the truth!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: That's a deal. Perhaps, behind the truth of it all, there lies a story more fantastical than any work of fiction.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like we just learned so much from Xingqiu! A drought, a nameless heroine, a life of seclusion... Wait, why does this story sound super familiar?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! There's a drought in this story, too. Um, Xingqiu, are droughts super common in Liyue or something?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Well... They used to be. But people have long since developed methods to prevent them, like by cultivating the soil or digging canals.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: So while droughts do happen from time to time, they are rarely regarded as true disasters. The drought fifty years ago is probably one of the worst we've had in the last several centuries.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: The crops withered, the streams ran dry, and the monsters in the mountains became rabid and agitated. Countless caravans were attacked, and people who lost their homes came together to form bandit groups... What started as a natural disaster soon became a human tragedy as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds awful...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Yeah, and that's exactly why the nameless heroine was so beloved. She must have been someone of true integrity, to do so much for the people while asking nothing in return.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Still, as terrible as that drought was, it was nothing compared to the truly calamitous disasters that befell this land in ancient times.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: They say that back in those days, disasters were both more severe and more common. Only the strongest of adepti could hope to dispel the ruin and devastation.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Do you have any other questions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're good for now! We're just going to head back and meet up with Ms. Xianyun and the others again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes that Granny Yuandai will be able to remember more of her past! She used to be a great hero who saved many people. It's so sad that she can't recall any of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we'll be off now! See you some other time, Xingqiu. Thank you so much for your help!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: It's no problem at all. Safe travels.

talks.objective: Meet up with the others at where Madame Ping is

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I have recorded the tune that you requested. I hope it will be of help to you.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Streetward... Ping, what has amused you so?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh, it's no serious matter. I was just reminiscing about the last time I saw you in this form... Time has wrought such change in this world, and yet, you appear just the same as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Time has little bearing on one's existence, nor has one keenly felt its effects whilst dwelling at Mt. Aocang. Nevertheless, Ping... One would like to seek your counsel on a personal matter.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh? Why so formal all of a sudden? I must say, you're making me a little nervous. What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Well... The inquiry is as such...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: ...Approximately how much Mora would one need to afford a comfortable life in the Harbor, not unlike the one that you yourself lead?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hmm... it does not require as much as you may think. Still, do you mean that—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cloud Retainer, Madame Ping! What are you two talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Ahem... Nothing, save for some trivial matters. Have you unearthed any useful details?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xingqiu has a theory... But let's save it for when Shuyu and Ms. Yuandai have joined up with us again.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Shuyu and Yuandai soon arrive at the scene. Paimon relays Xingqiu's theory...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Do not be troubled, young lady. Here, have some tea.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Ah... Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you think, Shuyu? Does it match up with what you know of your Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: According to the story, the nameless heroine eventually fell in love with an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng. Maybe... that's my grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I don't have many memories of him. But, there was this one time, I found a box in our attic full of a bunch of weird sigils.

choices.text: Seems like the stories were on the right track.

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: I think so too. Granny might remember something once she's returned to a familiar place.

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: What marvelous tea... I can taste the dew's sweetness in this cup.

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: It's as if I was taking a stroll in the mountains... thoroughly one with nature, and at peace...

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Is that so? Then please drink as much as you like. There's no need to hurry. At our age, it's always nice to slow down and take the time to appreciate pleasant conversation among friends.

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: Thank you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's rest here for a little while, then.

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: Okay. Since we have the time... Could I ask you something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! What would you like to know?

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: Um... I have a secret I wanna tell you. Let's go talk over there.

choices.text: We should probably pay a visit to the three places mentioned in the books.

talks.objective: Listen to Shuyu tell of a secret experience

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Shuyu?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Well, I've kinda been meaning to ask ever since we started talking in the restaurant, but are you guys all... adepti in disguise?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Uhh... About that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Well, you guys just seem super special. Plus... I think I might've heard Ms. Xianyun call herself an adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh... Must have been a slip of the tongue, hehe... Xianyun, since you were the one who, uh, "misspoke," maybe you can explain to Shuyu here what you really meant by that.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: One is indeed an adeptus. Is that of some concern to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I knew it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You don't sound surprised at all.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Well... One time when I was a little kid, I saw a pure white illuminated crane.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I had this super high fever, and Granny wasn't around. I was feeling all icky and gross. But then, this snowy-white crane flew down from the sky!

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: She put me on her back, and flew me to her cool adeptus house, and fed me some sort of magic potion. When I woke up, I was already back in my bed, and my fever was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I really wanted to thank her, but I was too sleepy to stay awake, so I never got the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: So, I just kinda wanted to ask if maybe... any of you have ever met an adeptus like that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A... pure white illuminated crane? The only two we've ever met are blue-and-white, and black-and-brown...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you ever met one that's pure white, Cloud Retainer?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Hmph. Never has one met an adeptus with such features. One surmises such a description is but a hyperbolic embellishment that oft results from narrative accounts.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: That's weird... Was it really just a dream, then?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Well, even if it was just in my head, it doesn't matter that much anyway — all I really want is to help Granny recover her memories. I'm really grateful for all your help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leave it to us! Now that we know the three locations, we just need to visit them one by one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go to Wangshu Inn first!

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Okay! I'll go get Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Wangshu Inn... Wangshu Inn...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Do you remember this place, Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Yes! The fish here is very delicious. And if you look out into the distance... you can always spot a bird that's been left behind by its flock.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I believe I used to have a room here. It had a window... Yes, yes, I spent a lot of time looking out that window. Which room was it again? Let me look...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I'll come with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's still having some trouble understanding what she's talking about, but if she's so familiar with this place, that must mean she lived here, right? Wait... Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah! Xiao! What are you doing here all of a sudden? You scared the living daylights out of Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I sensed a non-human presence and decided to come take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: If you're here, then there's likely no trouble afoot. I suppose there's no cause for concern.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...It's been a while, Cloud Retainer. I see you have returned to your previous form.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've met her in this form before?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I have indeed. I fought alongside her in this form on many occasions during the Archon War.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wow! What was she like during the War?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, let Paimon take a guess... Was it anything like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Behold the glory of one's newest invention, the Bang-Bang Continuous Fire Mechanism! Hands up in surrender, or be prepared to face the full might of the adepti!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: An impressive imitation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon knows her all too well!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Even so, Cloud Retainer was not always as ostentatious as you describe. You may be unaware, but her talent with adepti sigils is just as formidable as her skill in mechanics.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The Archon War reached its peak after Guizhong's death. The Cloud Retainer who fought beside me in those devastating battles was taciturn and solemn, only speaking when she had to activate her sigils.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A... Cloud Retainer who barely talks? Paimon can't picture it. But what happened after that? If you were so powerful in your human form, why did you decide to take up your bird form again?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Once one had bid farewell to the world of mortals, what use would one still have for such a shape?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: When dwelling between mountain and forest, away from the struggles and troubles of the mortal world, a mortal form is hardly the most fitting of choices.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: After the war, Cloud Retainer retired to Mt. Aocang, only revealing herself to the occasional visitor, and always in her avian form.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Although, I do believe there was an occasion some thirty odd years ago when she decided to don her human form. I believe it was for the purpose of—

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Ahem. One believes there is little need to relive bygone matters.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Granny! Are you okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Ahh... Back then, at this place, I...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Perhaps this conversation should end here. I shall take my leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Should you encounter any trouble, you need only call my name. However, given that you are traveling with Cloud Retainer, I trust you are in good hands.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Everyone, I—I think Granny is finally beginning to remember her past!

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Slowly now. Calm your mind, and recount what has been recalled.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: A long time ago, I... stayed here to recuperate from my illness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So what Xingqiu said was true? You did fall ill? Was that why you went into hiding?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I... don't remember. I'm very sorry, but I can't even remember the name of my illness. The only thing I can remember is that it took a great toll on me, and there was no cure for it.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I was confined to my room in Wangshu Inn, where I spent many days unconscious. I'd come to every once in a while and stare at the migrating birds outside the window. It was a solemn sight. I remember crying... but I'm not even sure I knew why...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: One day, I met a traveling merchant. Upon hearing of my illness, he sold me a bottle of Soul-Revitalizing Teapills.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: He told me that the pills were concocted using adepti blood and could be used to alleviate my symptoms. Sure enough, I made a full recovery. My illness remained dormant for several decades after that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the "dementia" you're suffering from now is actually...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but if your illness "remained dormant" for several decades, are you saying that... what you're going through now is just a relapse of what happened all those years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And it was all thanks to the pills that you managed to keep the symptoms in check? Ugh... Paimon's brain kinda hurts... Do you remember anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I don't. *sigh* Ahh... If only I wasn't so useless...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Hey, you're not useless! You've done so much for me, watched me grow up, raised me... How could you say that about yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Fret not, dear child. Granny was just a bit frustrated. That's all...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: The recovery of a person's memories is a gradual process. Finding pieces of one's past is always superior to not finding anything at all. Let us make haste to the next location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Next location... next location... Why don't we go to the area north of Jueyun Karst next?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There isn't really a landmark there, so where should we start? Oh, Paimon's got it! Let's check out the houses in the area first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all, if she was there for any length of time, then she would've stayed somewhere, right? Paimon's really got her thinking cap on today! At this rate, we'll recover all of Granny Yuandai's memories in no time.

talks.objective: Look for clues in northern Jueyun Karst

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Time erases everything. Even the greatest of heroes will have their legacy reduced to the small fraction of their deeds that were committed to paper.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But I think the magic of chivalric novels lies in the way you can catch glimpses of a noble soul from a few mere paragraphs.

talks.objective: Look for clues in northern Jueyun Karst

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you remember anything about this place, Granny Yuandai?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Let me think... I feel like I've been here before.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: But I don't think I stayed here too long. I might have just rested here briefly before continuing on my way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it... That's okay, there are still plenty of other places we can check!

talks.objective: Look for clues in northern Jueyun Karst

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about this place? Any memories?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I don't remember this place at all... I don't think I've ever been here before.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Still, I was thinking... This place feels perfect for a game of hide-and-seek.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why a game of hide-and-seek?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I'm not sure. Maybe it's because... I used to play that game a lot with Shuyu when she was younger.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Hmm, I don't remember playing it that much. Are you sure about that, Granny? We only played a few times, and we stopped once we realized I was no good at the whole seeking part.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Ah, is that so? Then I must be mistaken.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, not here, then... Let's try somewhere else.

talks.objective: Look for clues in northern Jueyun Karst

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees an abandoned house! Why don't we take a break over there?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: This place... It's...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Did you remember something, Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I... I remember. Shuyu... This is where your father was born.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: It was a moonless night. I had been injured, so your Grandpa was supporting me. We fled together, with some being in the fog behind us in hot pursuit...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I had exhausted my strength when the labor pains came on, so we took refuge in this house. Your Grandpa set up a barrier outside, but neither of us knew if it could hold the monsters back.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I remember that night... I remember falling to my knees, reciting a prayer over and over.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I alone am the source of this sin. Punish me as you wish for forsaking my oath, but spare my innocent child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sin? Oath? Did you do something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I don't know... I don't remember. I only remember praying in the darkness with all my strength, until the sun finally rose again, and the fog cleared out.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Eventually, the house was filled with the sound of my baby's first cries. That baby was your father. I remember... I clutched him tight to my chest and wept tears of joy. It was the first time I'd ever felt such happiness in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: My dad...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: He was my pride and joy, and so are you, Shuyu. You're so much like him, and I love you both so much...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: But you're... always going to be different from me. I... Why... Just what did I do?

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: I don't care what you might have done, Granny. You'll always be the person I love more than anything.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: You're too sweet, Shuyu. I'm lucky to have you with me... If not for you, I would not have had the courage to come here, to try to remember what I've forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Alright, let's not stand around any longer. There's one place left, yes? Let's go take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we're finally here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does this place feel familiar to you, Granny Yuandai?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: ...How strange. Have I... lived here before?

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: When we were at Wangshu Inn and the abandoned house earlier, though I couldn't remember everything, I still... felt a sense of familiarity. I could easily picture myself in those places...

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: But here... I don't have that feeling. Perhaps I did come here in the past, but it just didn't leave a strong impression on me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Did the stories get it wrong, then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can't expect them to get everything right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's true... But they're also the only thing we have to go off of.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was hoping this place would jog Granny Yuandai's memory just like the others.

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: I'm sorry to disappoint you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's alright! We're not going to give up yet! We'll figure something else out, just you wait!

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: Thank you. If only I could remember...

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: Huh? That way... What's that mountain?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, let Paimon look — huh!? Isn't that Mt. Aocang? Looks like we've come full circle!

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: Mt. Aocang... Mt. Aocang...

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: Granny? Are you okay?

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: Don't push yourself, Granny. It's okay if you can't remember... You shouldn't do something that makes you sad...

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: Mt. Aocang. I... What am I, really...

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Mt. Aocang holds some familiarity to you?

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: It does. But I... I can't go back...

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Are you feeling unwell?

response.speaker: Yuandai
response.text: My head... It feels all heavy and dizzy. Just what is wrong with me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cloud... Ms. Xianyun. Is there anything you can do...?

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Let us go to Mt. Aocang.

response.speaker: Shuyu
response.text: ...But—

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Fret not, all will be well. Yuandai, you have already given more than enough to the pursuit of this endeavor.

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: You may leave the rest to me. I've prepared something that can aid you in suppressing the fear in your heart and restoring your lost memories. It currently resides at Mt. Aocang.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, really!? When did you do that?

response.speaker: Xianyun
response.text: Hah, I never leave anything to chance. All will reveal itself when we arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As more and more guests begin to trickle in, Paimon takes the opportunity to order a whole array of delicious dishes...

dialogues.speaker: Baotai
dialogues.text: I've always wanted to try this place...

dialogues.speaker: Dixin
dialogues.text: For this price, the food is unbelievable!

dialogues.speaker: Wenliu
dialogues.text: Everyone, please eat to your hearts' content! Today is my treat.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: You can taste the sweetness of the dew?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: It's just a feeling — the sensation of stepping out into the mountains on a cool morning, gazing upon the small droplets of water hanging from the leaves, and feeling the sweet stream of water soothe a parched throat with every swallow...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: It's a sense of calm and serenity, one that stretches on and on, until days become weeks, weeks become years...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Leaving already? Well, just remember that you can come over for a cup of tea at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Where are you going, Granny? Don't you like the food?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Fresh milk... I need to buy you some fresh milk.

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Milk? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: You need to drink milk before eating, or the spicy food will make you cry. Hush, little one, don't cry...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyu
dialogues.text: Granny, you're forgetting things again! I'm not a little baby anymore — I can eat spicy food now. Even the super spicy dishes like their fish stew. I can eat two whole bowls, no problem...

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Wonderful, how wonderful... my darling granddaughter is all grown up...

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: I should get paid in another few days. Shall we take the opportunity to go out and have some fun?

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: This is one of our busiest periods in the year... Things should calm down a little in another few days.

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: I sure am glad to have Shenhe now. There's no way I'd have been able to cope this year all by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Why are there so many Treasure Hoarders here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Guess it's time to round up some bad guys, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Wait a second. If I remember correctly... I believe I brought... Ah yes, I brought some sweet snacks with me.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: Go on, take some. You need to eat a lot if you want to grow big and strong...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, thank you! Then Paimon will help herself!

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: If one recalls correctly, the next place should be Qingyun Peak. Yuandai, how fares your health?

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: I may be a bit slow, but I'll do my best to keep up. I'm sorry to keep everyone waiting...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Climb on. I shall carry you to the top.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: ...Such lightness of weight.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: All those who grow old grow frail in the end, do they not? First, you lose your memory, then your health. Eventually, you end up losing everything.

dialogues.speaker: Yuandai
dialogues.text: My only wish is to depart this world with a lucid mind, to free myself of this torment and the burden it places upon others...

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Fret not. You have my aid in this endeavor.
